items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: You talked about the main influences that came before you, Buddy, and Gene, which were Papa Jo... He taught me all about brushes, hi-hat – like Jo Jones, how to listen.

ctx.x: That was Sam, but I might not be right. I’ve been, maybe. Anyway . . .

Anyway, I was up there with Mel Lewis. We were talking together. Ippolito said, “Wish you guys stick around a little bit, because Papa Jo’s coming in.” I said, “Oh yeah. I can stick around.” Mel said, “I can stick around too.” In the interim, there’s 20 young kids – little kids. Ippolito doesn’t mind if they get on the drums. Let them have a ball. Sounded like a war going on. Brrrr, brrrrr, bang, bang, bang, bang, bang, brrrrr, brrrr. Can you imagine? 20 kids. Mel Lewis and I had to go in the office. We were…
What was it? Do you remember what it was?
